What you actually get

A reconditioned engine, rebuilt with your own parts

We supply a fully reconditioned engine block, then transfer your original accessories across onto it, so it drops straight into your vehicle. Here is how it comes together.

FAQs

Frequently asked questions

Quick answers to common questions about our engines and services.

Do you do urgent or emergency engine replacements?

Yes. We handle urgent and emergency engine replacement 24 hours a day for Hyundai, Kia and iLoad vehicles. A courtesy car can be arranged while your vehicle is with us, subject to availability, and we can organise towing to our Hallam workshop. Send us an itemised written quote for identical work from a legitimate workshop and we will beat it by five per cent.

How much does a Hyundai or Kia engine replacement cost?

It depends on your model, engine code and whether you need supply only or supply and fit. Send your rego or VIN and we will give you our best price fast, and we will beat any genuine written quote.

Do you deliver Australia-wide?

Yes. We supply reconditioned Hyundai, Kia and iLoad engines to every state and territory with fast delivery, and we fit engines at our Hallam, Victoria workshop and across VIC and NSW.

Can you fit my iLoad engine?

Absolutely, the iLoad is our specialty. With 300+ iLoad engines supplied and fitted, we know the 2.5L CRDi turbo-diesel inside out and offer urgent replacement to keep your business moving.

What engines do you supply?

Reconditioned petrol and diesel engines across the Hyundai and Kia range, including iLoad, iMax, i30, ix35, Tucson, Santa Fe, Palisade, Staria, Kona, Elantra and Sonata, plus Kia Carnival, Sportage, Sorento, Cerato and more.

How long does the process take?

Once we confirm the right engine, supply is fast and fitting is scheduled to minimise downtime. Tell us your vehicle and timeframe and we will give you a clear turnaround.

Do you use genuine or OEM quality parts?

Yes. We rebuild with OEM-grade parts and purpose-built tools, restoring engines to factory specifications, then test output, torque and fuel efficiency before release.
